calls.body: Since 2023-24, Wedgewood has been a wall against the Ducks, well above his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if the Ducks finally get to him.

calls.head: The Avalanche should drive the play
calls.body: The Avalanche have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Ducks near the bottom. Expect the Avalanche to spend more of the night in the Ducks’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

surprises.head: A shutout for Scott Wedgewood
surprises.body: Wedgewood stopped all 25 shots, worth 2.7 expected goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 40 starts.

story.head: Wedgewood slams the door on the Ducks
paras: Nicolas Roy and Brock Nelson scored a little over three minutes apart early in the second to put the Avalanche up 2-0. Nelson scored his second of the night midway through the period to make it 3-0, and Devon Toews stretched the lead to 4-0 midway through the third. The Ducks’ Stian Solberg played his first NHL game. Nelson added an assist for a three-point night.

The chances were closer than the score. The Ducks hit two posts and the crossbar, and the bounces never came. Scott Wedgewood turned aside all 25 shots for the Avalanche, and Lukáš Dostál stopped 23 of 27 at the other end. The Avs moved to 13-7-3, third in the Central, while the Ducks dropped to 11-11-1, third in the Pacific.

items.text: Cutter Gauthier’s twelve-game point streak ended.
With Nathan MacKinnon out, Nelson took his spot and scored twice and added an assist and won 10 of 16 faceoffs.
The Avalanche won without Nathan MacKinnon, Josh Manson, Cale Makar and others. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team was missing more at the time.
Mike Reilly made his Avalanche debut, after two seasons with the Hurricanes.
